cells.remarks: States that Muttuvīraṇavāthadēva, son of Kaṭṭadēva, who was the elder brother of the king and was residing at Uttarakōśamaṅgai, remitted half of the revenue from the villages Āykkudi and Sundaravūr which belonged to Tiruvēṅkaṭanāthayya, son of Tirumalai-nātha-Tiruvēṅkaṭāchārya for the expenses of feeding in the temple of Aḷagar and for digging a tank between the temple and Appan-Tirupati. cells.location: Patlavidu

cells.remarks: Fragment in characters of about the 11th century. Seems to be a copper-plate grant, of which this is evidently a copy. Registers grant of the village Rāmāḍuke in the Nagatana-koṇḍa-sīma by Timmari-Nāyaka, son of Yallari-nāyaka, a subordinate of the king, for the merit of the king. The chief is said to have got the Nāgatanakoṇḍa-sīma as nāyankara from Krishṇarāya-Mahārāya, and the grant was made on the banks of the Krishṇaveni during a lunar eclipse in the presence of god Virūpākshadēva.

cells.place: On the wall of Muktīśvara †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Svasti śrī [kō]chchaḍaiya[varmma]ṇ, etc. Registers sale of land to the temple of Paraśurāmēśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār by certain residents of Tiruvaṅgalam in Kaḷār-kūṟṟam, a subdivision of Uḷaguda-iyā-Nāyaṉār-vaḷanāḍu, as a tax-free gift for the maintenance of taxes, adjoining the above, by the assembly. In conti-nuation of this inscription is another dated in the 12th year, Vrischika, śu., ēkādaśi, Thursday, Rēvati, which registers a gift of land for a lamp by the same assembly. Begins with the introduction [Svasti śrī] kōchchaḍaiya[varmma]ṇ, etc., of Kūḷōttunga I. The characters are late and the surname 'Pāraśēśvararvarman' is wrong. Registers sale of land made tax-free to the temple of Tirumaṅgalam-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār by the assembly of Tirumaṅgalam who are stated to have met for the purpose in the temple of [Tiru]aly [ō]ttiyal-var in the village.

cells.remarks: Continuations of lines lost. Begins with the introduction Pugalmāduviḷanga, etc. Records the sale of land, made tax-free, by two residents of Tirukkuḍavāyil, a brāhmaṇa in Taḷaināḍu in Kuḍa-nāḍu, a subdivision of Uṭṭama-Chōḷa-vaḷanāḍu in Rājarāja-Pāṇḍināḍu to a certain Chōḷa-kōn of the same place for the temple of Somanāthadēva. Gift of land in Arumolidēva-vaḷanāḍu of Chōḷa-maṇḍalam, who made a gift of it to the temple of Sōmanāthadēva for the sacred bath of the deity with water from the Tappuṇḍam (Tāṇḍapāḍi). Above this inscription is a record of the 3rd year of the Pāṇḍya king Māravarman alias king Śrīvallabha beginning with the words Śrī-kō-chchaḍaiya-panmar, etc.

Begins with the introduction [Śōḷar]kula-tilaka, etc. Records gift of money for a lamp to the temple of the [ir]uḍichchēram-uḍaiyār, the images of Oḷakka-Viṭaṅkar and Nityasundara in the temple of Sōmanāthadēva alias Ten-Tiruppūvaṇam-Uḍaiyār at Aṭṭūr, a brāhmaṇadēya in Kuḍu-nāḍu, a subdivision of Uttamaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu in Rājarāja-Pāṇḍināḍu, by a servant of the vāsal of Kaḷattūr-nāḍu-maṅgalam alias Śivantalai, a brāhmaṇadēya in the same rāḍe with himself as the tenant. Slightly damaged and built in in the middle. Begins with the introduction [Śōḷar]kula-tilaka, etc. The record refers to the gift of land by the assembly of the [Kōṭṭūr] on the lands at Tiruchchirambalamudaiyār in Koḍukāi-nāḍu, for offerings to the deity.

cells.location: TIRUCHCHENDUR TALUK
cells.place: On the wall of Somanātha-svāmi †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines in the latter portion built in. Begins with the introduction Tirumagal-pōla, etc. Seems to register sale of land tax-free to the assembly of Kīḷār-kūrram for the temple of Mahādēva at the temple of Rājarāja-viṇṇagar-Pallikoṇḍaruḷinadēva (Vishṇu), Durgā-Bhagavatī, Saptamātris, Kaḷētrapāla and Gaṇapati, set up in the temple of Sōmanāthadēva alias Ten-tiruppuvanam-uḍaiyār at Ārūr-Śōḷamādēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam. The land was purchased and recorded in the 27th year of the king, which records gift of sheep for a perpetual lamp to the temple, by an archer of the king named Adhiran Sendil. Records gift of sheep by a Vellala of the village, for a perpetual lamp to the same temple.

cells.remarks: Mutilated. Praises one Śrīrāma-Daṇḍanātha, the son of Somasēkhara and a subordinate of the king. Also refers to the conservation of the liṅga called Kapila-Siddha-Mallikārjunadēva (probably Mallikārjuna) by a Brahmana (name lost). Probably Mentions the Dōsiya-gaṇa, ṅgaiyavaṇ, Chanīdirikridēva and Jayakīrtidēva. Contains the following labels:— (1) Aparājitadēva, (2) Bāhula-Yakshi, (3) Pātalā-Yakshi, (4) Kubēra-Yakshi, (5) Mahāmanasī-Yakshi, (6) Anantamati, (7) Õṁ-kāra, and (8) [Śa]ntanābhavaṁ.

Śaka 117[8], Nala, Pushya, ba. 30, Monday, solar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkramaṇa.
The details are not correct for Nala, in which year there was no solar eclipse on Pushya, ba. 30, nor did this tithi fall on Monday. Chālukya Vikrama year 11, Kahaṇa, Āshāḍha, śu. pūrṇimā, Sunday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 72: Śaka 9[3]6, Ānanda, Mārgaśira, ba. amāvāsyā, Tuesday, Vrischika-saṁkrānti
In Ānanda, Vrischika-saṁkrānti coincided with Tuesday, on Kartika-amāvāsyā and not on Mārgaśira-amāvāsyā. The month Mārgaśira is clearly the Pūrṇimānta month which is sometimes cited in southern records (cf. Ind. Ant. Vol. XXV, page 298). The corresponding English date is A.D. 1014, October 26, Tuesday.]

cells.place: Stone in the Rāmalinga temple
cells.date:
8th year, Jāvana, Pushya, su. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 74: 8th year, Īśvara, Pushya, śu. 10, Monday
Īśvara would be the 8th year for three kings, viz., (1) the Western Chālukya king Trailōkyamalla (Nūrmadi-Taila III), (2) the Yādava king Siṅghaṇa (according to Fleet) and (3) the Yādava king Rāmachandra. In Īśvara, falling in Nūrmadi-Taila's reign, Pausha, śu. 10 fell on a Friday; in Siṅghaṇa's reign, the tithi fell on Saturday; and in Rāmachandra's reign, it fell on Tuesday.
But in Siṅghaṇa's reign in Īśvara, Pausha, ba. 10 fell on a Monday. Assuming that śu. 10 is a mistake for ba. 10, the record might be assigned to his reign and the date would correspond to A.D. 1217, December 25, Monday. The characters do not militate against this assignment.]

cells.date: Vaiśākha, Vyatipata. 10th year, Prabhava, Chaitra, ba. 5, Monday, Vishu-sankrānti, Vyatipata.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Western Chalukyas from king Trailokyamalla and praises the king's subordinate, Mahamandalēśvara Sōmideva-rāja, governor of Banavāsi-1200, Madhuvidya and his son Somarāja-chānakya who built a trikūta temple at Muttage and at Vijayapuram. Records the gift, by the king, of the village of Nagasvada, in Mūgālu sthala, to the god Sivalinga at the aforesaid Trikūta temple, on the occasion of Uttarāyana-sankrānti. Given in detail the spiritual heirarchy of Lakuļīśvara who actually received the gift. Records also the subsequent grant of certain taxes (dampāyadaya) and certain dues (muru-gampu) by certain local Mahilars. Who was, a subordinate of Rijjaladevi, governing the Eroduvādi-nadu. Certain arjus also made gifts of money to the temple of Sivalinga while the king was camping at the capital, and to it. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XV, p. 26.

cells.place: the slab of Siddharāmayya †
cells.date: Pārthiva, Āshādha, ba. 10, Thursday, Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 110: Pārthiva, Āshāḍha, ba. 10, Thursday, Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti. Considering the sequence of the inscription on the slab, Parthiva might be taken to be the first Pārthiva coming after A.D. 1142. But the tithi on the day of Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti was not Āshāḍha, ba. 10, but it was śu. 5; and the saṁkrānti commenced only on the following Friday. But in the next Pārthiva (i.e., A.D. 1225), the Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti actually began on Thursday, June 26. This might be the corresponding English date though the tithi was not Āshāḍha, ba. 10, but ba. 5.]
cells.remarks: Registers the remission of the bennigidere tax on the garden of the same temple by Bommarasa-Danāyaka, son of Kīrtideva. Thousand of the gadyāna, (vens) kuranasa as paramāsundarati. Mentions the Mahājanas of the Brahmapurī of the god and the arani-pattiga (tenant) of the garden, Hammama, who was to supply the ghee and oil-mills, necessary for the lamps of the god. The settiguttas and nakhara of Muttage contributed 1daṇḍike, etc., required for the festivals of the deity, while the Mahājanas granted one oil-mill together with one gāṇagitti (oilwoman).

cells.place: Broken slab standing near the entrance to the Masjid.
cells.remarks: This is a composite record registering several facts and gifts. Prases king Subhātungavallabha born in the Rāshtrakūta-kula and mentions Krishna II and Kanhavallabha who are respectively the name and surname of Krishna II, who is also called Krishnarāja in the inscription. States that his subordinate Hirayamma-Sangata built a temple and made provisions for worship and offerings and some land to it. Subsequently, when this temple fell into ruin a Sūyavatisāmand Mōrudevimani renovated it and consecrated in it the two deities of Siddheśvara and Śiva. Some time later the king's feudatory Gundayya, son of King Jagadeamalla of the Chalukya line descended from King Nūrmadi Tailapa, by Chikabbe, the daughter of four curtain Mahāga Makamayya. Gifts made by the four curtain mahājanas of the palace, the gaudas, the setties, the Airanyanīru and Vaji-vardhana, by the residents of the village and the Three-Hundred Vajjani/ligas are also recorded.

text.remarks: This is a composite record registering several facts and gifts. Prases king Subhātungavallabha born in the Rāshtrakūta-kula and mentions Krishna II and Kanhavallabha who are respectively the name and surname of Krishna II, who is also called Krishnarāja in the inscription. States that his subordinate Hirayamma-Sangata built a temple and made provisions for worship and offerings and some land to it. Subsequently, when this temple fell into ruin a Sūyavatisāmand Mōrudevimani renovated it and consecrated in it the two deities of Siddheśvara and Śiva. Some time later the king's feudatory Gundayya, son of King Jagadeamalla of the Chalukya line descended from King Nūrmadi Tailapa, by Chikabbe, the daughter of four curtain Mahāga Makamayya. Gifts made by the four curtain mahājanas of the palace, the gaudas, the setties, the Airanyanīru and Vaji-vardhana, by the residents of the village and the Three-Hundred Vajjani/ligas are also recorded.Read more (1 KB)

cells.location: Bailur
cells.place: Slab standing near the Hashara huts.
cells.remarks: Records the gifts of lands, etc., made by Adhikāri Sanṇa-Nayaro and the several people of Bailur, viz., 10 Gadyāṇas towards the recitation of the Purāṇa daily in Nārāyaṇa-matha at Masakēśvara and also the gifts made to the same donee by Surēśvara-Śrīpāda and the several people, for expounding the Purāṇa on the 30 days of the month of Srāvaṇa in the maṭha of the Śrīpāda. The M.hāpradhāna Purōdhitāchārya is stated to have been ruling over the Tula-deśa having the capital at Barakūru. Contents are almost the same as the above record.

cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gives the genealogy of the king from king Saṅgama down to him and records that the king's mahāpradhāna ..... Refer to the Tuṅgabhadrā which formed, moat, as it were, to the city, to the nagarī Hasināvati, a temple of Rāmachandra and an āchārya called Rāmachandra-Yatiśvara. R-gisters gift of the village Chittarige in Honnāvūru-dēśa, for the benefit of the temple of Rāmachandradēva. Much damaged. Unfinished. Seems to refer to a chief called Vīra-Baṇaviya ... who belonged to the race of Jayakēśī and styled himself 'lord of Banavāpura' and regiters grant of land, house, house-site, etc., in the village of Chittarige in Kunbhataya-nādu. Records also a gift of land made by sixteen Brāhmaṇas to Hēra to certain Sabus who belonged to the Saurāshṭra country.

[Śaka 1282,] Vikāri, ... (Wednesday), Anurādhā. [date-calculation appendix, No. 120: Śaka 1282, Vikāri, . . . . . ., Wednesday, Anurādhā
In Vikāri, only on three occasions did Anurādhā combine with Wednesday, i.e., (1) 23rd October, f.d.n. '37, (2) 20th November and (3) 18th December in A.D. 1359. The intended date must correspond to one of these.]
